extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, university teachers, clergy, and learned students concerned with method and religious proofs
extracted.subtask_description: Advice and methodological prescriptions for using experimental natural philosophy (observation, experiments, modest use of hypotheses, attention to final causes) to establish truths about nature and to counter atheism and irreverent speculation. Emphasises pedagogical practice, academic conduct, and evidential standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use experimental demonstration to correct conceit
rubrics_metrics.description: Let them be brought into a Chymizcal Laboratory, or other Places where People are wont to make Phyſical Experiments, ſuch as are not commonly known to every body, and let them be asked what will be the Reſult of ſuch, or ſuch an Operation, purſuant to their own Notions and Conceptions? In which, if they miſtake, and Things appear quite contrary to what they expected, they can have no Subterfuge or Evaſion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring those who overvalue their own understanding into direct contact with experiments they are not familiar with; asking for predictions exposes mistakes and prevents evasion. Purpose: show the narrowness of their understandings by confronting fancied knowledge with empirical results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enquire experimentally into the true state and nature of things
rubrics_metrics.description: It is neceſſary to enquire experimentally into the true State and Nature of Things, and afterward to form a right Notion of them from thoſe Proof which are drawn from undeniable Experiments, and frequently to meditate upon the fame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use repeated, undeniable experiments as the basis for forming correct notions of natural phenomena; combine observation with reflection to appreciate the power and wisdom evident in nature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid deducing everything from a single hypothesis
rubrics_metrics.description: The wrong Way of Thinking may be aſcribed to the Manner of Deducing all the Phenomena of Nature from a certain Hypotheſis... This Hypothetical Philoſophy... obliges Men to fancy that they have attained to a fundamental Knowledge of even the moſt principal Things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not substitute hypothetical stories for experimental proof; beware that multiple hypotheses can account for the same effects and that commitment to a favored hypothesis can corrupt judgement and lead to irreverent conclusions about God's wisdom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use hypotheses prudently as provisional tools
rubrics_metrics.description: We would not, however, that Men ſhould believe from hence, that we reject all Hypotheſes as quite unneceſſary; ſince, if they be properly ugſed, they are of great Service in many Caſes ... provided it be done with ſuch Prudence and Caution as may lead them to make a juſt Diſtinction the one and the other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat hypotheses as useful for organizing thought and instructing youth, but always with caution: distinguish clearly between hypothesis and demonstrated fact, and be ready to abandon hypotheses when experiments contradict them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer 'I know not' rather than feign knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: When we are asked about Things of which our Ideas are not sufficiently clear, [we should] anſwer calmly, and without bluſhing, I know not, and by no means pretending by this, or that unſeaſonable Account thereof, for fear of loſing the Reſpect that belongs to us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cultivate learned ignorance (Eruditum Nescire): admitting ignorance in unclear cases prevents pretence, maintains esteem among wise men, and fosters humility about the limits of one's understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not banish consideration of final causes entirely
rubrics_metrics.description: The Maxim that ... in Philoſophiſing, no Notice is to be taken of previous Deſigns or final Cauſes... if ſuch a Rule be admitted without any Reſtrictions, it may ſerve to miſlead Men into a raw Conception, that all Things are made without a View or Deſign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While final causes may not belong to the mechanical explanation of how things operate, consideration of uses and ends (scopology) can be a legitimate and valuable part of natural philosophy and may reveal wise design and new useful functions (examples: Harvey, Malpighi, Borelli).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use experiments as the characteristic marks of truth
rubrics_metrics.description: The beſt Way ... to avoid, and put an End to Diſputes, is to make uſe of ſuch Proofs ... that have their Foundation ... in undeniable Experiments, ſo often as it can be done. ... the greateſt Men of this laſt Age have allowed Experiments to be the only Characteriſticks of Truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer experimental/ocular demonstration over purely argumentative proofs to resolve disputes; many longstanding debates in natural philosophy have been ended by decisive experiments (e.g., blood circulation, air pressure in pumps, vacuums).

rubrics_metrics.name: Agree on marks/characteristics of truth and declare doubtful when marks are obscure
rubrics_metrics.description: Seriouſly to ſet about enquiring wherein the juſt Characteriſtick, or Mark of the Truth or Falſity of a Propoſition or Enunciation conſiſts: For if People did but agree in this one Thing, they might ... judge with Certainty of a Propoſition ... and if it had the contrary Marks, they might pronounce it falſe : And again, if thoſe Marks were obſcure on both Sides, they would declare it doubtful and uncertain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish common evidential standards so controversies can be settled or identified as genuinely uncertain instead of prolonged by cavilling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid abusing academic disputation about divine matters; handle with reverence
rubrics_metrics.description: Diſputes ... have given Occaſion to many to cavil about the moſt weighty Truths; ... you ſhall often hear them in publick Diſputes, arguing with as little Reſpect and Humility about the Being of a God, as concerning the vaineſt ... This inſenſibly engages them in a ſad Cuſtom of vainly uſing the tremendous Name of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prevent young minds being corrupted by irreverent public disputations on God: consider forbidding use of God's name/attributes merely as material for public exercise; teach such truths privately and with prayer so as to preserve reverence and avoid fostering contempt or Atheism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cure heedlessness by attending to new discoveries and experiments
rubrics_metrics.description: The only natural Means ... to render us more attentive to every thing, is frequently to apply ourſelves to new Diſcoveries and Experiments, which appearing to us upon every Essay to be New and Uncommon, do give us an Occaſion of obſerving with Aſtoniſhment the Wiſdom, Power and Goodneſs of Him that orders all Things.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combat natural sloth/carelessness and the blinding effect of custom by regularly engaging with new observations and experiments to renew wonder and attention to the Creator's works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer proofs from God's works (natural philosophy) over metaphysical arguments for many audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: It may be inferred, that the exact and experimental Obſervations of what we ſee in the World, is a demonstrative Means ... to attain to the Knowledge of a Gop and his Perfections by his Works: ... The Reaſons ... are: First, many learned Perſons have unanswerably confuted the Atheists after a Metaphyſical Manner; Secondly, Experience and Converſation ... has taught me, that the Contemplations of God's Works ... has induced ſome among them to alter their Sentiments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For persuading wavering minds (and as scripture itself models), use plain, observational arguments from nature rather than abstruse metaphysical proofs; such proofs are more accessible and effective for many audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject authoritative speculative descriptions of the universe unsupported by experiment
rubrics_metrics.description: I refer ... to ſuch ſort of Books ... which pretend to give a true Notion of the whole Frame and Conſtruction of the World ... with as much Aſſurance as if they had been preſent ... Now, if ſo be that any Man ſhould fall into ſuch an unhappy Opinion, as to receive for 'Truth all that he finds written in ſuch Books, how can he do otherwiſe than believe, that there was no more Wiſdom requiſite to bring this glorious Frame of the World into ſuch a beautiful Order ... than what the Authors of ſuch Books were Maſters of?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be suspicious of books that confidently describe the entire universe without grounding in experiment: they can mislead youth and diminish reverence by making God's work seem no greater than clever human speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infer divine agency from the multiplicity, order, regularity, and purposive behaviour of phenomena
rubrics_metrics.description: If one ſhould ... conſider, Firſt, in caſe he had ...: 1. Not one, but a great many, 2. And-various or different, 3. Things entirely ignorant, or unknowing of all, and even of themſelves too: 4. Each of them frequently after a particular Manner; 5. However always unchangeably, and obſerving the ſame Rule ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To form a proof of God's existence from the visible world, note the number, variety, ignorance, regular behaviour and uniform rules governing things; these features combined point to a wise, powerful, and designing Cause. (This is the sketch of the general demonstrative method to be applied to particular phenomena.)
